chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who remembers the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he is in the prescribed prayer, either bowing or prostrating, so he sends blessings upon him while he is in that state. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. The sending of blessings upon the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is like the form of the Takbir and the Tasbih, and it is ten good deeds, which eighteen angels compete to deliver to him.'
ai.seo_question: Can one send blessings upon the Prophet while bowing or prostrating in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that sending blessings upon the Prophet during Ruku' or Sujood is valid and spiritually potent, equating its merit to the fundamental acts of Takbir and Tasbih. It highlights the celestial dimension of this practice, noting that ten rewards are generated and expedited to the Prophet by eighteen angels, underscoring the continuous connection between the worshipper and the Prophet even during the physical postures of prayer.
